correctness.rationale: Jacobi moments m2=1/(2r+1), m4=3/[(2r+1)(2r+3)] reconstruct the exact jump derivative. The absolute-affine integral gives its complete s-profile. The stationary quartic has exactly the two required interior roots because the off-center test beats the centered value and endpoints, leaving a unique positive maximizing root. The beta/Stieltjes integral representation extends the sharp step norm to every BV input; a single jump attains it. Large and small weight limits follow from explicitly expanded root and gamma quotient. Symbolic computations, 45 independent weighted jump integrals, BV-stress, and limiting tests passed from packaged script; experiments do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The weighted symmetric-Jacobi least-squares family is canonical in spectral approximation. A one-parameter exact norm and rigid optimal jump location resolve how the first genuinely curved projection amplifies total variation; a nonmonotone small-weight regime and asymptotically linear high-weight instability quantify robustness beyond the already known single unweighted number.
